rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation entails innate true cognition, including monotheism; deviations misuse innate faculties rather than abolish their built-in orientation.
rows.anchor: فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that pure rational inquiry is unreliable because it often errs relies on rational premises and so cannot coherently refute reason; error reflects misuse of reason.
rows.anchor: الأبحاث العقلية المحضة، والقياسات المؤلفة من مقدمات بعيدة من الحس يكثر وقوع الخطأ فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Empirical arguments for trusting sense and experiment also depend on rational premises, so they cannot use reason to cancel reliance on reason.
rows.anchor: والدليلان كما ترى سيقا لإثبات وجوب الاعتماد على الحس والتجربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Experiments, analogy, and personal approval cannot establish revealed laws; broad moral principles are innate, while their detailed prescriptions must come through revelation.
rows.anchor: والقرآن يبطل ذلك كله بإثبات أن الأحكام المشرعة فطرية بينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an forbids following what one does not know or Satan's steps, and calls the revealed law truth; speculation cannot replace it.
rows.anchor: ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since what lies beyond truth is error and God does not guide the astray, false or unjust means cannot yield truth, justice, goodness, or piety.
rows.anchor: فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an bars reflection detached from piety; it pairs legal instruction with moral virtues that awaken piety and help people understand the ruling.
rows.anchor: يحظر على الناس التفكر من غير مصاحبة تقوى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses al-ajl as a crime or offense.
rows.anchor: في المجمع الأجل في اللغة الجناية

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines al-ajl as an offense whose later consequences are feared: every ajl is a crime, but not every crime is an ajl.
rows.anchor: الأجل الجناية التي يخاف منها آجلا، فكل أجل جناية وليس كل جناية أجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author traces min ajli from causal reference to an offense or fault to a general expression meaning because of.
rows.anchor: ثم استعمل للتعليل، يقال فعلته من أجل كذا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report from Abu Jaʿfar says envy led Qabil to stalk and kill Habil secretly; its longer account also treats Adam's later succession and the prophets' legacy.
rows.anchor: عن حبيب السجستاني، عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال لما قرب ابنا آدم القربان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's apparent account is that Qabil killed Habil by stealth, without Habil enabling the attack; al-Tabataba'i says this better fits reflection and his prior discussion.
rows.anchor: وظاهرها أن قابيل إنما قتل هابيل غيلة من غير أن يمكنه من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Narrations call the brothers Habil and Qabil, while the circulating Torah has Habil and Qayin; the Torah naming has no evidentiary force because its chain ends with an unknown person and its text is altered.
rows.anchor: اسم الابنين هابيل وقابيل، والذي في التوراة الدائرة هابيل وقايين

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: In a report from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, Habil offered a prized ram and Qabil a sheaf; Satan taught Qabil to smash Habil's head with stones, and a raven taught him burial, after which Adam mourned and received Hibat Allah (Shith).
rows.anchor: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام يحدث رجالا من قريش قال لما قربا ابنا آدم القربان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls this report middling and textually confused: Qabil's prior threat seems inconsistent with not knowing how to kill; he reads the uncertainty as not knowing which method to choose.
rows.anchor: الرواية من أوسط الروايات الواردة في القصة وما يلحق بها وهي مع ذلك لا تخلو عن تشويش في متنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports transmitted by Sunni and Shiʿi routes have content close to the al-Qummi account.
rows.anchor: وهناك روايات أخر مروية من طرق أهل السنة والشيعة يقرب مضمونها من مضمون هذه الرواية

rows.speaker: روايات
rows.claim: One report says God kept Habil's ram in Paradise for forty years before it became the ram sacrificed by Abraham in place of Ishmael.
rows.anchor: إن الله أخذ كبش هابيل فخزنه في الجنة اربعين خريفا

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: روايات
rows.claim: Another report says Habil let Qabil kill him and refrained from raising a hand against his brother.
rows.anchor: والقائلة أن هابيل مكن قابيل من نفسه وانه تحرج ان يبسط يده إلى أخيه

rows.speaker: روايات
rows.claim: One report says Qabil's leg was fixed to his thigh for life; in winter he was enclosed in ice and in summer in fire, attended by seven angels in succession.
rows.anchor: والقائلة ان قابيل لما قتل أخاه عقل الله إحدى رجليه إلى فخذها

rows.speaker: روايات
rows.claim: Another report says Qabil is tormented upside down on an island in the sea until the resurrection.
rows.anchor: والقائلة انه معذب في جزيرة من جزائر البحر علقه الله منكوسا

rows.speaker: روايات
rows.claim: Another report says Qabil hangs by his horns in the sun, turning with it through its freezing and scorching extremes until the resurrection, then enters Hell.
rows.anchor: والقائلة ان قابيل بن آدم معلق بقرونه في عين الشمس تدور به حيث دارت

rows.speaker: روايات
rows.claim: One report identifies the killer of his brother as Qabil, who had been born in Paradise.
rows.anchor: والقائلة ان ابن آدم الذي قتل أخاه كان قابيل الذي ولد في الجنة

rows.speaker: روايات
rows.claim: Another report says Adam lamented Habil in several Arabic verses.
rows.anchor: والقائلة ان آدم لما بان له قتل هابيل رثاه بعدة أبيات بالعربية

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: روايات
rows.claim: Another report claims their law required a person targeted by an attacker to let the attacker do as he wished without resistance.
rows.anchor: والقائلة انه كان من شريعتهم ان الإنسان إذا قصده آخر تركه وما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects these and similar reports as mostly or entirely weak, inconsistent with sound reflection and the Qur'an, and likely fabricated, distorted, or corrupted in transmission.
rows.anchor: فهذه وأمثالها روايات من طرق جلها أو كلها ضعيفة

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report transmitted from ʿUmar says the Prophet advised someone facing a would-be killer to act like the better son of Adam: the victim is in Paradise and the killer in Hell.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم " يعجز أحدكم أتاه الرجل أن يقتله

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Abu Musa tells believers during civil strife to break their swords, cut their bowstrings, stay indoors, and be like the better son of Adam.
rows.anchor: عن البيهقي عن أبي موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال " اكسروا سيفكم يعني في الفتنة

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Jarir and ʿAbd al-Razzaq from al-Hasan says the two sons of Adam exemplify this community, which should follow the better of them.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جرير وعبد الرزاق عن الحسن قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These fitna reports read Habil's statement as surrendering to Qabil and refusing self-defense; al-Tabataba'i rejects that reading because sound reports and Qur'an support defending oneself and truth, including fighting a transgressing faction.
rows.anchor: الآثار الصحيحة الآمرة بالدفاع عن النفس والانتصار للحق

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i distrusts these narrations because their transmitters included people who sat out the civil strife and ʿAli's wars; they should be reinterpreted if possible, otherwise discarded.
rows.anchor: في حروب علي عليه السلام مع معاوية والخوارج وطلحة والزبير

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the reading that Habil enabled Qabil to kill him and left himself undefended.
rows.anchor: بأن المراد تمكين هابيل لأخيه في قتله وتركه الدفاع، وقد عرفت ما فيه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from ʿAli attributes to the Prophet the statement that Qasiyun, a mountain in Damascus, is where Adam's son killed his brother; al-Tabataba'i regards this report as acceptable.
rows.anchor: عن علي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: A report from Kaʿb al-Ahbar identifies alleged blood on Mount Qasiyun as the blood of Adam's son.
rows.anchor: روى بطريق عن كعب الأحبار أنه قال إن الدم الذي على جبل قاسيون هو دم ابن آدم

rows.speaker: عمرو بن خبير الشعباني
rows.claim: Amr ibn Khubayr al-Shaʿbani reports seeing a flowing streak on the mountain with Kaʿb, who identified it as the blood-mark left where Adam's son killed his brother.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن خبير الشعباني قال كنت مع كعب الأحبار على جبل دير المران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suspects the mountain's alleged blood trace is folklore planted to draw visitors for pilgrimage, vows, and gifts, like fabricated marks and graves.
rows.anchor: ويشبه أن يكون ذلك من الأمور الخرافية التي ربما وضعوها لصرف وجوه الناس إليها بالزيارة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report from Abu Jaʿfar defines the profligate as those who deem inviolable things permissible and shed blood.
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام المسرفون الذين يستحلون المحارم ويسفكون الدماء

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Genesis 4 presents Cain and Abel's offerings, Cain's murder of his brother, the curse and mark placed on Cain, and his departure to Nod.
rows.anchor: فقال الرب لقايين أين هابيل أخوك؟ فقال لا أعلم أحارس أنا لأخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i urges readers to compare the Torah's account of the brothers with the Qur'an's account and judge the differences.
rows.anchor: وعليك أن تتدبر ما تشتمل عليه القصة على ما قصتها التوراة وعلى ما قصها القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the Torah portrays God anthropomorphically as an earthly human who approaches, speaks to, withdraws from, and hides from people; God is exalted above this.
rows.anchor: فأول ما يبدو لك من التوراة انها جعلت الرب تعالى موجودا أرضيا على صورة إنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That portrayal implies humans once lived face to face with God and that God later hid from Cain, contradicting human sameness and God's transcendence of material conditions.
rows.anchor: مع أن البراهين القاطعة قائمة على أن الإنسان نوع واحد متماثل الأفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an assumes humans are alike and uses the raven's burial of another raven to show humanity's gradual development through sensory and intellectual learning.
rows.anchor: وأما القرآن فإنه يقص القصة على أساس تماثل الأفراد غير أنه يذيل قصة القتل بقصة بعث الغراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habil's dialogue conveys innate religious knowledge: monotheism, prophethood, resurrection, piety, injustice, divine law, and God's justice in acceptance and afterlife recompense.
rows.anchor: ثم يذكر محاورة الأخوين فيقص عن المقتول من غرر المعارف الفطرية الإنسانية وأصول المعارف الدينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story ends with the killer's remorse and loss, then explains that murdering one person is like murdering all humanity and saving one is like saving all.
rows.anchor: ثم يبين بعد ذلك كله أن القتل من شآمة أمره أن الذي يقع منه على نفس واحدة

rows.speaker: جماعة من مفسري القوم
rows.claim: Some exegetes treat these verses as continuous with the bans on alliance and read wilaya as support, restricted to God, the Messenger, and true believers; they connect them to 3:68, 33:6, 8:72, and 9:71.
rows.anchor: جماعة من مفسري القوم إشتراكهما مع ما قبلهما وما بعدهما

rows.speaker: جماعة من مفسري القوم
rows.claim: On that reading, the specified believers are the true faithful, excluding hypocrites and the sick at heart, and the verse assigns them mutual support with God and the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء هم المؤمنون حقا فيخرج بذلك المنافقون والذين في قلوبهم مرض

rows.speaker: جماعة من مفسري القوم
rows.claim: To explain while bowing in the support reading, some interpreters take bowing figuratively as humility before God or as a condition of poverty and need when giving alms.
rows.anchor: بحمل الركوع على معناه المجازي وهو مطلق الخضوع لله سبحانه أو انحطاط الحال لفقر ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects a unified context: although the surah was revealed late, its verses came down at different times, as their content and occasions of revelation show; adjacency does not prove common occasion or context.
rows.anchor: فليس مجرد وقوع الآية بعد الآية أو قبل الآية يدل على وحدة السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding passage forbids believers' alliance with Jews and Christians and criticizes hypocrites for seeking their favor without addressing those communities; the following passage directly addresses the forbidden groups, so their purposes differ.
rows.anchor: فالغرض في القبيلين من الآيات السابقة واللاحقة مختلف، ومعه كيف يتحد السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior passage's clauses that each group are one another's allies and that an ally becomes one of them do not fit a mere support pact; they describe affectionate alliance and spiritual-social assimilation.
rows.anchor: بخلاف عقد ولاية المودة التي توجب الامتزاج النفسي والروحي بين الطرفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative reading of bowing makes the verse say that believers' guardians are God, the Messenger, and faithful worshippers who submit to God's lordship in obedience, or give alms while poor.
rows.anchor: ويعود معنى الآية إلى أنه ليس أولياؤكم اليهود والنصارى والمنافقين بل أولياؤكم الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is improper to call the Prophet a supporter of believers in the relevant religious sense; support is rendered to God's religion, which God legislates and the Messenger and believers uphold.
rows.anchor: على أنه ليس من الجائز أن يعد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وليا للمؤمنين بمعنى ولاية النصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an calls the disciples helpers of God and describes support for God's cause and covenant with prophets to believe in and support the coming messenger.
rows.anchor: قال الحواريون نحن أنصار الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an also praises the Prophet's supporters, those who aid God's Messenger, and the Helpers who sheltered and supported the emigrants.
rows.anchor: وعزروه ونصروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since believers are bound to God's religious law, the Qur'an describes God as supporting those who support Him and as supporting His messengers and believers.
rows.anchor: ولينصرن الله من ينصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion cannot belong only to believers with the Prophet outside it and then make him their supporter: he shares every religious distinction in its fullest measure, and the Qur'an never calls him their supporter.
rows.anchor: ولا في آية واحدة، وحاشا ساحة الكلام الإلهي أن يساهل
